title: RelayShield's Agentic Attack Surface Is Now an MCP Server

html:
AI agents get compromised differently than humans do. A typosquatted MCP server, a prompt-injection attack that exfiltrates credentials, an agent framework sitting on an unpatched CVE, a service-account identity nobody's watching. These aren't edge cases anymore, they're the actual attack surface for anything running autonomously.

We've been building toward this all year under the "Agentic Attack Surface" focus area. It is the same technology behind our recent AgentCore/x402 work, where we proved an autonomous agent could discover and pay for a real security check entirely on AWS's own infrastructure. Today we're shipping the next piece: four of those checks, live as an MCP server anyone can add to their client.

The four tools:

  • MCP Server Risk : Typosquat detection, criminal IOC corpus match, domain-registration age for any MCP server URL

  • Prompt-Injection Breach Check: Flags credential exposure specifically sourced from prompt-injection attacks, distinct from ordinary phishing/malware

  • Tech Stack CVE Check: CISA KEV / high-EPSS CVEs targeting your declared agent framework (LangChain, CrewAI, AutoGPT, n8n self-hosted, and their common companion infra)

  • Bulk Identity Risk: Hierarchical org + agent-identity risk scoring, built for AI agent governance and MSP client sweeps

Add it from your Hugging Face MCP settings, or find it directly: huggingface.co/spaces/relayshieldadmin/relayshield-agentic-attack-surface. Each call needs your own RelayShield key. Get it self-serve at api.relayshield.net/developers, billed only for what you use.
